title: Figma library publish gating: variant sanitization, token reconciliation, and auto-layout fixes
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Introduce an automated publish gate and follow-up cleanup work for the Figma component library that prevents broken/duplicate variants, enforces semantic spacing/color tokens, and normalizes auto-layout constraints for buttons, tables, and chart primitives before any library publish. The goal is to reduce regressions introduced by ad-hoc edits and decrease downstream engineering churn when consuming the library.
background: Over the last two sprints we've observed several regressions after library publishes: duplicated variant states, orphaned local tokens, inconsistent padding on button sizes, and chart legends that detach at narrow widths. Manual QA catches some issues but it's slow. We need a combination of design cleanups, naming conventions, and an automated gating step (Figma plugin + CI check) to block publishes until key checks pass.
acceptance_criteria: A Figma publish attempt is blocked by CI if any of the automated checks fail (plugin returns errors).
All color and spacing tokens in the library are reconciled to the semantic token map (no unresolved raw tokens remain).
No component has more than one instance of a variant with identical name/visuals (duplicates deduped or flagged).
Primary/secondary/tertiary button variants share consistent auto-layout settings (padding, vertical alignment, min-width).
Table row and cell components use fixed constraints and responsive auto-layout so table resizing doesn't collapse chart cells.
Chart primitives (legend, axis, series) have documented responsive rules and constrained auto-layout so narrow widths stack instead of breaking layers.
A manual publish checklist is codified in the repo and referenced in the Figma file; design sign-off step is required for P0/P1 token changes.
tasks: Audit token map: run token export and reconcile raw tokens -> semantic tokens; create migration plan for 12 tokens used in charts and tables.
Variant sanitization sweep: run duplicate detector, mark duplicates for merge, and create rename map for inconsistent state names.
Auto-layout normalization: update buttons to use fixed vertical padding (8px top/bottom) and token-driven horizontal padding; set min-width for medium/large sizes.
Chart primitives cleanup: anchor legend and axis groups with 'Hug contents' + fixed spacing tokens; add responsive stacking prototypes.
Publish gate plugin: collaborate with Eng to surface plugin results via GitHub Actions; plugin should return JSON report and non-zero exit on failures.
Document publish checklist and recovery steps in DESIGN/README and link to automation runbook.
Run a canary publish to a test library and validate SDK consumers (storybook / internal dashboard) for visual regressions.
Collect feedback from two product teams consuming charts and tables and iterate on token adjustments.
decisions: Adopt semantic spacing tokens (spacing-xx) as single source of truth — remove component-level hardcoded pixel paddings where feasible.
Fail-fast approach for publishes: CI will block publishes for P0/P1 token changes without explicit lead designer sign-off; smaller cosmetic changes allowed with automated pass.
Prefer renaming and merging variants instead of keeping parallel variant sets to reduce consumer complexity.
Plugin will treat 'duplicate variants' as errors but provide an optional auto-merge flag; auto-merge will require manual review in this sprint (disabled by default).
tradeoffs: Stricter gating increases friction for quick fixes but reduces time engineers spend debugging downstream regressions.
Automated merges could inadvertently remove intentionally divergent variants; conservative approach chosen to flag rather than auto-merge initially.
Normalizing auto-layout may change some micro-spacing; will be coordinated with PM and feature owners to avoid UX surprises.
risks: Large token migration may cause small visual deltas across several product surfaces — requires cross-functional signoff and a staged rollout.
Plugin false-positives could block legitimate publishes; will include an override workflow for emergency publishes after manual review.
Resource constraints: Eng availability for plugin CI integration is limited this sprint — may push some ops to follow-up cycle.
notes: Created a draft semantic token map spreadsheet and shared with the design guild (link below).

We will scope the plugin to run 7 checks initially: token mapping verification, duplicate variant detection, auto-layout constraint check, frame naming standard, missing component description, orphaned local styles, and chart legend anchoring.
Diego will prepare a patch branch that runs the plugin as part of 'figma-publish' GitHub Action; Marina will own the design checklist doc.
